# Introduction to Stochastic Processes {#intro}

The course will cover the probabilistic framework for stochastic models
of real-world applications with emphasis on actuarial work. We will
illustrate some practical actuarial problems for which we will develop
mathematical models, tools and techniques for analysing and quantifying
the uncertainty of the problems.

## Why Stochastic Processes?

Many quantities encountered in actuarial science, finance, engineering, and the natural sciences evolve over time. Some evolve in a predictable manner, whereas others are affected by chance. A stochastic process provides a mathematical framework for describing such random phenomena.

Consider the following questions.

* How many insurance claims will have occurred by time $t$?
* What No-Claim Discount (NCD) level will a policyholder be assigned at the next policy renewal?
* Will a policyholder aged 70 survive to age $70+t$?
* What will be the price of a stock one week from today?

## Example

::: {#exm-ncd}

## No-Claim Discount (NCD) System

A **No-Claim Discount (NCD) system** is widely used in motor insurance to adjust a policyholder's premium according to their recent claims experience. A policyholder who remains claim-free is rewarded with a premium discount, whereas one or more claims may result in a reduction of the discount or an increase in premium.
:::



## Callout

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Idea

A stochastic process is **not** a single random variable. It is a **collection of random variables**, where each random variable describes the state of the system at a particular time.
:::
